progress: Movement, an instrument aimed at the cash economy rather than at payment
summary: The Bank of Eritrea [gave holders of cash outside the banking system until 31 July 2026 to deposit it](2026-07-02 Eritrea's banking ultimatum - deposit cash by 31 July 2026), on pain of legal action.
developments:
2026-07-02 — a legal notice from the Bank of Eritrea [ordered cash held outside banks deposited by 31 July 2026](2026-07-02 Eritrea's banking ultimatum - deposit cash by 31 July 2026), with legal action threatened against holders who do not comply. The notice defines no threshold for the excessive holding it names and states no enforcement mechanism.

It is the only central-bank action on this ledger, and it addresses the cash economy rather than any payment system.

2026-09-09 - a further Bank of Eritrea legal notice, No. 134/2026, [caps cash an individual may keep beyond 15 days at 25,000 nakfa and private institutions at 50,000 to 150,000 by grade](2026-09-18-eri-martinplaut-new-cash-restrictions), in force on publication. It is known through a human-rights group's statement, which records no cash machines or cards and thin branch access outside the main towns; what counts as an acceptable reason, and the penalty, are not defined.
qualifier: central bank cash-deposit notice only; payment-systems mandate not on record

summary: UNDP's [statistical-capacity grant](2019-01-01-undp-eri-data-stats-2019-economic-social-data-development-eritrea) runs to 2026, beside [US$14.02m of education grants](2024-04-19-gpe-eri-001-eritrea-emis-system-transformation-grant) committed in 2024.
developments:
The standing position is a US$1,676,837 UNDP grant to the Government of Eritrea and the National Statistics Office, [committed in 2019 with an end year of 2026](2019-01-01-undp-eri-data-stats-2019-economic-social-data-development-eritrea). Nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 records a disbursement, an extension or a successor, and no disbursement figure for it is published. The grant funds the statistical work reported under Censuses and surveys, so what movement there is shows up there rather than here.

A second development partner is on the ledger after all: the Global Partnership for Education committed US$14.02m to the education ministry through UNICEF as grant agent in April 2024, for a foundational-learning reform programme including work on the education management information system ([grants](2024-04-19-gpe-eri-001-eritrea-emis-system-transformation-grant)).

progress: Movement, on the ministry's own figures
summary: The ministry reports [about 73km of new cable laid and landline plant renovated in six towns](2026-05-19 Eritrea substantial investment in communication service expansion); no independent measure of the backbone exists.
developments:
2026-05-19 — the minister responsible for communications [reported 184 towers installed, about 73km of new cable laid, and landline plant renovated in six named towns and at the Naval Force Base](2026-05-19 Eritrea substantial investment in communication service expansion), against a claimed cumulative investment above 35 billion Nakfa.

The figures are the ministry's own, carried by state media, and nothing on the ledger tests them: no operator disclosure, no regulator return and no third-party measurement of the network appears for Eritrea in the window. EriTel remains the sole operator.
qualifier: minister's claims of towers and 73 km new cable; backbone reach or absence not on record

progress: Movement, on a ministry figure, with no cable landing behind it
summary: Bandwidth is [reported at about 1,536 Mbps after a decade of growth](2026-05-19 Eritrea substantial investment in communication service expansion), and it is carried by satellite: [no submarine cable lands in Eritrea](2026-04-16 The Long View - What ICT4D did for Africa and why that deep past matters for today).
developments:
2026-05-19 — the ministry [put international bandwidth at about 1,536 Mbps, risen over the past decade](2026-05-19 Eritrea substantial investment in communication service expansion).

2026-04-16 — the industry position is unchanged: Eritrea [is still the only one of Africa's coastal states with no cable landing](2026-04-16 The Long View - What ICT4D did for Africa and why that deep past matters for today), and cable firms describe a country that does not answer landing requests. [An earlier account of the same position](2024-06-10-cable-firms-eye-eritrea-red-sea-houthi-attacks) dates it to June 2024.

EriTel's international transit therefore runs on geostationary satellite, which is what a bandwidth figure of this size describes. The growth is real and the ceiling is the technology carrying it.
qualifier: no cable landing; international transit on geostationary satellite

summary: Starlink [lists Eritrea with no planned launch date](2026-07-17-starlink-launches-27th-african-country-ivory-coast), one of seven African states without a timetable; the repository holds no licence application or refusal.
developments:
2026-07-17 — Starlink's own availability map [still lists Eritrea as having no planned launch date](2026-07-17-starlink-launches-27th-african-country-ivory-coast), leaving it one of seven African states with no announced timetable, all of them in North Africa and the Horn. The position is the one the repository carried at the start of the window.

What is not on the ledger is any Eritrean decision: no application, no refusal and no regulatory statement about satellite broadband appears, so the absence is recorded from the operator's side only.
qualifier: Starlink lists no planned launch; no licence application or refusal on record

summary: Active connections [reached 859,000, or 23.7% of the population, up 8.2% year on year](2025-11-08 Digital 2026 Eritrea (DataReportal)), among the lowest rates in Africa.
developments:
2025-11-08 — DataReportal's Digital 2026 report for Eritrea [puts active mobile connections at 859,000, 23.7% of the population, 49.3% of them broadband, and up 8.2% on the year](2025-11-08 Digital 2026 Eritrea (DataReportal)). [The previous edition](2025-03-03 Digital 2025 Eritrea (DataReportal)) is the comparison.

The direction is upward and the level is among the lowest in Africa. Both statements are true, and the second governs what sits downstream of it: a foundational digital ID, mobile money and any service assumed to reach a citizen through a handset all rest on this figure. No operator or regulator return on the ledger tests it.

Coverage is separately reported and much higher than connections: [85% of the population is covered by a mobile-cellular network but only 35% by at least third-generation service and 0% by at least fourth-generation](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile), on 2023 international figures. Nearly a quarter of the population holds a connection inside a network that reaches five-sixths of them.

summary: ASYCUDA World [was inaugurated in January 2026](2026-01-08 Eritrea launches ASYCUDA World digital customs system), replacing customs software dating from 2007, with the source code transferred to the government.
developments:
2026-01-08 — [ASYCUDA World entered service](2026-01-08 Eritrea launches ASYCUDA World digital customs system), replacing customs software in use since 2007. UNDP supported the implementation and the source code was transferred in full to the Eritrean government, which is the part worth recording: the system is nationally held rather than run on the country's behalf.

It is the only sectoral management information system on this ledger, and nothing states what it connects to — no revenue system, no business register and no trade single window appears for Eritrea.
qualifier: ASYCUDA World in service from January 2026; posts covered and single window not on record

summary: The repository holds [no operational foundational digital ID](2025-07-26 Eritrea's population digital identity - challenges ahead), a position profiled in July 2025 and untouched since.
developments:
2025-07-26 — a digital identity index profile [found no operational foundational identity system](2025-07-26 Eritrea's population digital identity - challenges ahead) and set out what one would face: low connectivity and mobile penetration, thin digital infrastructure, a telecom monopoly and weak civil registration.

Nothing in the twelve months to 2026-08-26 changes that. No enrolment programme, procurement, pilot or legal instrument on digital identity appears on the ledger, so the standing position is carried forward on a single profile written just before the window opened.
qualifier: 2025 identity index finds no operational digital ID; handwritten card being replaced by an electronic one

summary: With [no foundational digital system in service](2025-07-26 Eritrea's population digital identity - challenges ahead), the credential is a [card issued since 1992, handwritten until 2014](2018-09-26-eritrea-national-id-card-ecoi).
developments:
The same 2025-07-26 profile that finds [no operational foundational identity system](2025-07-26 Eritrea's population digital identity - challenges ahead) names weak civil registration among the barriers a future one would face, which is the nearest the repository comes to a statement about coverage.

No enrolment figure exists to report, because there is nothing to enrol into. The population counting the repository does hold is the survey work reported under Censuses and surveys, which is a statistical exercise and not a register.

The credential that does exist is documented: [identity cards are issued by the Department of Immigration and Nationality, were first issued in 1992 and were handwritten until 2014, with applicants submitting a municipality letter, a birth certificate and proof of citizenship to one of twelve branch offices which forward the application to headquarters for approval](2018-09-26-eritrea-national-id-card-ecoi). A [newer electronic card carries a laser-engraved photograph, the holder's fingerprint and a unique serial number](2018-09-26-eritrea-national-id-card-ecoi), and [citizens aged 18 and over are required to hold one](2024-10-17-eritrea-embassy-national-id).

No issuance volume, coverage rate or database behind the card is on record at any date, and the fullest account of the system is eight years old.

summary: [Eri-Chat, an offline AI application built by a ministry developer](2025-11-01 Eri-Chat offline AI app), launched in April 2025 and was shown at an Asmara diplomatic event in October.
developments:
2025-11-01 — a profile of the developer Naod Goitom Isaac [describes Eri-Chat, an offline AI application launched in April 2025](2025-11-01 Eri-Chat offline AI app) and shown to ambassadors and UN officials at an Asmara UN Day event on 24 October 2025. It works in English only; local-language support waits on training data the developer says does not exist in sufficient quantity.

It is one application written by a single software developer at the Ministry of Information rather than a national programme, and it is the only AI system of any kind on this ledger.
qualifier: one locally built offline app; not shown to be a national model; no funding or usage

summary: A self-organised collective [released five Tigrinya-language education applications](2026-08-15-eritrea-shambko-apps-group-local-language-education) built to the national curriculum, with no stated funding or distribution channel.
developments:
2026-08-15 — an interview carried by the state information ministry [describes five applications from the Shambko Apps Group](2026-08-15-eritrea-shambko-apps-group-local-language-education): literacy, puzzle, cultural-heritage and arithmetic tools written against the national curriculum, with a stated plan to extend them to Eritrea's eight other national languages.

The group is a private collective rather than a state programme. Nothing is stated about download counts, distribution channel or funding, and no hub, incubator, investor or company registration appears elsewhere on the ledger — so this is one collective on the record, not evidence of a startup base.
qualifier: A self-organised app collective is on record; no startup law, strategy or support scheme, and no cited absence

summary: The fourth [Eritrea Population and Health Survey completed fieldwork in 9,794 households](2026-05-08 Eritrea strengthens data systems with EPHS 2025 (UNDP)) across all six regions, with the report due in 2026.
developments:
2026-05-08 — the National Statistics Office [reported the fourth Eritrea Population and Health Survey complete: 9,794 households across 405 enumeration areas, a 98.4% household completion rate, and collection by computer-assisted personal interview](2026-05-08 Eritrea strengthens data systems with EPHS 2025 (UNDP)).

Around 400 tables over 20 chapters are drafted, with writing, printing and dissemination scheduled through 2026, so the fieldwork is finished and the published output is not. Technical support came from UNECA and an Oslo consultancy under the UNDP-led Joint Programme on Data for Development. It is the most substantial statistical work the repository holds for Eritrea.
qualifier: 2025 health survey completed, first in fifteen years; no census on record

summary: The statistics office [compiled national accounts for 2023 and began collection for 2024](2026-05-08 Eritrea strengthens data systems with EPHS 2025 (UNDP)), the only administrative statistical production the repository records.
developments:
2026-05-08 — alongside the household survey, the National Statistics Office [is reported to have compiled the 2023 national accounts and started data collection for 2024](2026-05-08 Eritrea strengthens data systems with EPHS 2025 (UNDP)).

That is the whole of the ledger's evidence on statistics drawn from administrative sources, and it is second-hand: the accounts themselves are not on the repository, and no statement of which administrative systems feed them appears either. No statistics law and no national strategy for the development of statistics is on record for Eritrea, so this production rests on the office's own practice.
qualifier: survey and national accounts only; administrative sources neither shown used nor stated unused

summary: A verification pass dated August 2026 confirms no comprehensive data-protection law in force ([redetermination](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection)).
developments:
A dated redetermination as of 1 August 2026 confirms the position is unchanged: no comprehensive data-protection law in force, no supervisory authority established and no enforcement decisions published ([redetermination](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection)).

A regional ministerial assessment places Eritrea's data-protection policy area at a nascent stage without legislation or regulatory oversight, grouped with Djibouti, South Sudan and Sudan against neighbours that have enacted frameworks with supervisory authorities ([policy matrix](2025-09-01-hoai-digital-policy-matrix-update-data-protection-nascent)).

A trade regulatory profile records that Eritrea lacks a comprehensive legal framework for data protection, with no data-protection officer, impact-assessment or retention requirements ([profile](2022-01-01-uneca-dtri-eritrea-digital-trade-regulatory-country-profile)).

This is a searched absence rather than an unexamined one: three independent assessments across four years agree.
qualifier: No data protection law; absence reconfirmed on a 1 August 2026 verification pass

summary: No supervisory authority exists and none is provided for; the position was re-verified in August 2026 ([redetermination](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection)).
developments:
The August 2026 verification pass records no comprehensive data-protection law, no supervisory authority and no published enforcement decisions ([redetermination](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection)).

The Communication Department, the only body empowered to supervise and regulate the communication sector, has little to no decision-making authority on a trade regulatory profile ([profile](2022-01-01-uneca-dtri-eritrea-digital-trade-regulatory-country-profile)).

The nearest legal anchor is the privacy article of the 1997 Constitution, which has never been brought into force ([legal status](2026-06-08-levellers-ai-regulation-eritrea)).

Readiness here is not partial: there is no law, no regulator and no route to redress.
qualifier: No law, no authority, no ratification; absence cited and reconfirmed August 2026

summary: The [2015 Penal Code provides for computer crimes](2015-05-15-eritrea-penal-code-2015-computer-offences) but [had not been enacted by April 2026](2026-07-22-acerwc-concluding-observations-eritrea); no cybercrime statute exists.
developments:
The 2015 Penal Code was drafted to provide for computer crimes ([Penal Code](2015-05-15-eritrea-penal-code-2015-computer-offences)), and the children's rights committee recorded in April 2026 that it had not yet been enacted ([observations](2026-07-22-acerwc-concluding-observations-eritrea)).

A country cybersecurity assessment records, item by item, no cybercrime legislation, no cybersecurity regulation, no officially recognised national computer incident response team, no national cybersecurity strategy, no governance roadmap and no responsible agency ([assessment](2015-03-12-eritrea-itu-cyberwellness-profile)).

Nothing in the window changed either position: the code is not in force, and the institutional apparatus a cybersecurity regime needs does not exist.

Nor is there a strategy behind the missing statute: a country profile records [no public national cybersecurity strategy](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile), so neither the legislative nor the policy layer exists on the record.
qualifier: computer offences only in the 2015 Penal Code, published but not enacted at April 2026

summary: No freedom of information law has been adopted, a UN review body states plainly ([review contribution](2026-01-01-unesco-upr46-eritrea-freedom-of-information)).
developments:
A formal contribution to Eritrea's universal periodic review states that no freedom of information law has been adopted, that the 1997 constitution guarantees access to information, and that the 1996 press proclamation requires all media to be licensed and publications approved before release ([review contribution](2026-01-01-unesco-upr46-eritrea-freedom-of-information)).

The 2026 world press freedom index places Eritrea last of 180 countries and territories for the third consecutive year ([index](2026-05-01-rsf-world-press-freedom-index-2026)).

The absence is legislative and practical at once: there is no statute, no request procedure and no appeal route, so nothing measures how much information is released.
qualifier: UN review contribution states no freedom of information law adopted

summary: A press-freedom index places Eritrea last of 180 for the third consecutive year ([index](2026-05-01-rsf-world-press-freedom-index-2026)).
developments:
The 2026 world press freedom index places Eritrea last of 180 countries and territories for the third consecutive year, alongside China and North Korea, describing a state of press freedom that has hardly changed ([index](2026-05-01-rsf-world-press-freedom-index-2026)).

A United Nations commission of inquiry found a complex, multi-layered system of surveillance of the population inside and outside the country, used to instil fear and keep it under control ([findings](2015-06-05-un-coi-eritrea-detailed-findings-chapter-vi)).

There is no forum on the record — no independent press, no permitted civil society, no online space — in which digital or data policy could be publicly argued.
qualifier: No independent press or public forum; last of 180 on the 2026 press-freedom index

summary: No electronic transactions framework is in force; a legal-reform project publishes consultation drafts not presented as enacted law ([drafts](2026-01-01-the-abc-journey-draft-laws-commercial-code)).
developments:
A legal-reform project published around eighty consultation-draft acts, codes and regulations showing how Eritrea's legal order could be reconstructed within the 1997 Constitution ([drafts](2026-01-01-the-abc-journey-draft-laws-commercial-code)). They are prepared for public debate and not presented as enacted law.

The standing assessment is that Eritrea has not adopted the model laws on electronic commerce and electronic signatures and has no legislation giving electronic signatures legal equivalence ([profile](2022-01-01-uneca-dtri-eritrea-digital-trade-regulatory-country-profile)).

Nothing on the repository records a government bill, a consultation or a stated intention to legislate on electronic transactions.
qualifier: no e-transactions framework in force; 2026 consultation drafts not shown to include an e-transactions bill

summary: A review dated June 2026 records no dedicated artificial-intelligence law and no national strategy ([review](2026-06-08-levellers-ai-regulation-eritrea)).
developments:
A legal-status review dated 8 June 2026 states that Eritrea has no dedicated artificial-intelligence law, no national artificial-intelligence strategy, no data-protection statute and no data-protection authority, and that the nearest legal anchor is the privacy article of the 1997 constitution, which has never entered into force ([review](2026-06-08-levellers-ai-regulation-eritrea)).

The absence is total rather than partial: no instrument, no draft and no institution with a mandate.
qualifier: June 2026 legal-status review found no AI law

summary: A June 2026 legal-status review records no published national artificial-intelligence strategy ([review](2026-06-08-levellers-ai-regulation-eritrea)).
developments:
A June 2026 legal-status review records the same absence from the legal side: no national artificial-intelligence strategy ([review](2026-06-08-levellers-ai-regulation-eritrea)).

The repository does hold one AI system in state hands — an agricultural expert system inside a ministry information system — so the absence is of policy, not of the technology.
qualifier: June 2026 legal-status review found no national AI strategy

summary: No digital-identity statute exists; the closest instrument is the 1992 nationality proclamation ([proclamation](1992-04-06-eritrea-nationality-proclamation-21-1992)).
developments:
No dedicated digital-identity statute was located. The closest identifiable legal instrument is the Nationality Proclamation 21/1992, still in force, which provides the legal basis for nationality certification through the Department of Internal Affairs and contains no digital-identity, electronic-identity, biometric or electronic-transactions framework ([proclamation](1992-04-06-eritrea-nationality-proclamation-21-1992)).

Identity cards are nonetheless required by other systems: anti-money-laundering law obliges financial institutions to set customer identification policies ([proclamation](2014-09-08-eritrea-aml-cft-proclamation-175-2014-id-kyc)), and a national identity card is required before a passport is issued ([country guidance](2026-03-02-uk-gov-eritrea-knowledge-base-profile)).

So the card carries statutory weight without a statute defining it, and nothing regulates what data it holds or who may read it.
qualifier: 1992 nationality law in force; no row shows it establishing the ID system or authority

summary: The statistics office has never operated under an enacted statistics law; a draft proclamation was recorded as pending ([review](2007-01-08-norad-eritrea-nso-statistics-norway-mid-term-review)).
developments:
A mid-term review of statistical capacity support records that the statistical proclamation, the equivalent of a statistics act, had been submitted to government and that the formal issue was still pending ([review](2007-01-08-norad-eritrea-nso-statistics-norway-mid-term-review)).

No later record of enactment was located at the probe date of 31 August 2026, so the national statistics office has operated for at least two decades without a statutory mandate.

This matters for the surveys the repository does hold: a population and health survey was carried out without a law defining who owns the data, who may access it or on what terms it is published.
qualifier: draft statistical proclamation recorded pending in 2007; no enactment located since

summary: Standardisation rests on the 1995 proclamation establishing the standards institution as sole national organ ([proclamation](1995-09-20-proclamation-75-eritrean-standards-institution)).
developments:
The Eritrean Standards Institution was established by proclamation in 1995 as an autonomous body with legal personality and the sole national organ for standardisation, quality assurance and metrology, with powers to prepare compulsory Eritrean standards, affix conformity marks, test and certify import and export products, and inspect ([proclamation](1995-09-20-proclamation-75-eritrean-standards-institution)).

Nothing in the window amended that proclamation, and the repository holds no Eritrean standard made under it that bears on digital systems, data formats or interoperability.

The institution exists and its output in this field is not on the record.
qualifier: standards body exists; no ICT or data standard or quality policy on record

summary: The 1995 standards proclamation adopts the international system of units as the legal measurement system ([proclamation](1995-09-20-proclamation-75-eritrean-standards-institution)).
developments:
The proclamation establishing the Eritrean Standards Institution expressly adopts the International System of Units as Eritrea's legal measurement system ([proclamation](1995-09-20-proclamation-75-eritrean-standards-institution)).

A structured government-technology dataset for 2022 records no government enterprise architecture framework, no government interoperability framework and no data quality framework ([dataset](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech)).

So metrology is aligned to international standards and government data practice is not; nothing on the repository records adoption of an international standard for identity, payments or data exchange.
qualifier: standards body exists; ISO membership and adopted international standards not on record

summary: Population registration runs on six separate regional registers with no central national register ([technical description](2021-01-21-swiss-sem-focus-eritrea-digital-population-registers)).
developments:
Eritrea's population registration has been digital at regional level since 2001: six separate registers, one per zoba, each recording an identity number, family and resident numbers, nationality and civil data, from which residence cards and family identity cards are printed as extracts. Birth registration feeds them through the local family register. There is no central national register ([technical description](2021-01-21-swiss-sem-focus-eritrea-digital-population-registers)).

A regional treaty body, reviewing Eritrea's fourth periodic report in April 2026, recognised the development of a five-year strategic civil registration and vital statistics plan for 2024-2028 ([concluding observations](2026-07-22-acerwc-eritrea-concluding-observations-crvs)).

A country-of-origin report carries a dedicated section on the register and the cards drawn from it ([report](2023-12-31-netherlands-eritrea-country-origin-information-report)).

The repository holds no coverage rate and no statement that the six registers reconcile with one another.
qualifier: decentralised zoba registers per a 2021 foreign-government report; updating from vital events not on record

summary: Birth registration feeds the regional population registers, and a national identity card is required before a passport is issued ([guidance](2026-03-02-uk-gov-eritrea-knowledge-base-profile)).
developments:
Operational country guidance published in March 2026 states that Eritrea issues national identity cards and that a national identity document is required before an Eritrean passport can be issued ([guidance](2026-03-02-uk-gov-eritrea-knowledge-base-profile)).

Birth registration feeds the zoba population registers through the local family register and transfer documents, and the identity and residence cards are printed extracts of those registers ([technical description](2021-01-21-swiss-sem-focus-eritrea-digital-population-registers)).

The chain therefore exists but is regional rather than national, and the repository holds no birth-registration coverage rate, so how many children enter it is not known.

What feeds them is not measured: the [2025 vital statistics return leaves birth and death registration completeness blank](2025-01-01-eritrea-2025-vital-statistics-metadata-questionnaire), and the only structural account, from 2002, records [registration under a transitional civil code in eight urban areas only, optional rather than obligatory, kept for administrative purposes with no statistical data retained](2002-10-21-eritrea-demographic-profile-birth-registration). An identity layer fed by a registration system of unknown coverage inherits that unknown.
qualifier: zoba population registers and a CRVS plan on record; register-to-ID exchange not described

summary: The statutory business register is still operated manually, with no registration website and clearance through six offices ([assessment](2025-10-14-eritrea-focus-state-dept-ics-2024-business-register)).
developments:
An investment climate assessment records that Eritrea has no business-registration website and requires manual registration and clearance through six government offices ([assessment](2025-10-14-eritrea-focus-state-dept-ics-2024-business-register)).

The register itself is statutory: a 2002 proclamation requires the trade ministry to establish and maintain a business information register covering trade, manufacturing, services, fisheries and commercial farming, specifying the fields collected, annual reporting obligations, penalties and judicial review ([proclamation](2002-12-27-eritrea-business-information-register-proclamation-124)).

A register that exists in law and on paper is a different thing from a digital one, and nothing on the repository records the register being computerised or published.
qualifier: external assessment: no registration website, manual registration through six offices

summary: Land registration rests on the 1997 proclamation establishing the cadastral office, with no statement of its operational extent ([proclamation](1997-05-19-eritrea-proclamation-95-1997-land-registration-cadastral-office)).
developments:
The 1997 land registration proclamation established the Cadastral Office under the land, water and environment ministry, responsible for registering all land, rights over land and transfers of property, following the 1994 change of tenure under which all land belongs to the state with allocable private rights ([proclamation](1997-05-19-eritrea-proclamation-95-1997-land-registration-cadastral-office)).

The proclamation establishes the office and not the register's reach. The repository holds no parcel count, no coverage figure and no statement that the register is held digitally.
qualifier: cadastral office in law since 1997; operational extent not on record

summary: The electoral law provides for a voter register, and nothing records one ever having been compiled ([electoral law](2026-06-08-eritrean-electoral-law-constitutionnet)).
developments:
The hosted electoral law, its proclamation number left blank, establishes an independent electoral commission and defines a voter register and voting cards ([electoral law](2026-06-08-eritrean-electoral-law-constitutionnet)).

The repository holds no record of a national election held under it, no commission constituted and no register compiled. The hosted text of the law is itself undated.

This is a register that exists as a statutory design and not as a system.
qualifier: no election since 1993; register only in a draft law, never compiled on record

summary: Eritrea does not appear on the postal union's list of countries operating a postcode system ([reference](2026-08-01-upu-general-addressing-issues)).
developments:
The Universal Postal Union's addressing reference, dated August 2026, does not list Eritrea among the countries that require or use a postal-code system, establishing that no national postcode system exists ([reference](2026-08-01-upu-general-addressing-issues)).

The document does not itself state whether any other national addressing scheme operates, and the repository holds nothing else on the question — no street-naming programme, no digital addressing initiative and no geocoding of the population registers.
qualifier: Absent from the postal union's postcode list; postcodes are not the whole addressing system, so no absence of addressing is cited

summary: An action plan to domesticate the UN geospatial information framework was filed with the regional economic commission in April 2026 ([action plan](2026-04-06-uneca-eritrea-domesticated-igif-action-plan)).
developments:
An action plan to domesticate the United Nations Integrated Geospatial Information Framework for Eritrea was filed with the regional economic commission's data and geospatial section on 6 April 2026 ([action plan](2026-04-06-uneca-eritrea-domesticated-igif-action-plan)).

The position it moves from is comprehensive absence: a 2022 structured assessment records no government enterprise architecture framework, no government interoperability framework, no data quality framework and no government service bus platform ([dataset](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech)).

The plan is geospatial in scope rather than whole-of-government, and the repository holds no adoption date, budget or implementing body for it.
qualifier: only a geospatial framework action plan on record; no government interoperability framework or cited absence

summary: The only planning record touching data governance is a geospatial framework action plan filed in April 2026 ([action plan](2026-04-06-uneca-eritrea-domesticated-igif-action-plan)).
developments:
An action plan to domesticate the geospatial information framework was filed in April 2026; its content is not held ([action plan](2026-04-06-uneca-eritrea-domesticated-igif-action-plan)).

Against it, a 2022 structured assessment records no data quality framework and no system exchanging data across financial management, human resources, customs, tax or social insurance ([dataset](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech)), and there is no data-protection law or authority ([redetermination](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection)).

A sectoral plan is not a national data-governance policy, and nothing on the repository claims one exists.
qualifier: only a geospatial framework action plan on record; no national data policy or cited absence

summary: No law enables data exchange between government systems; a 2022 assessment records no service bus and no cross-system exchange ([dataset](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech)).
developments:
A structured government-technology dataset for 2022 records no government interoperability framework and no system that exchanges data across financial management, human resources, customs, tax or social-insurance systems ([dataset](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech)).

A regional ministerial assessment places Eritrea's data-protection policy area at a nascent stage without legislation or regulatory oversight ([policy matrix](2025-09-01-hoai-digital-policy-matrix-update-data-protection-nascent)), so there is also no legal basis on which systems could lawfully share personal data.

The one system that did move is closed rather than connected: the customs platform runs on an intranet architecture independent of continuous internet access ([account](2026-01-08-undp-eritrea-asycuda-world-digital-customs)).
qualifier: only a customs platform on record; no data-sharing instrument or cited absence

summary: The national laboratory built genomic sequencing capacity and applied it nationally to malaria and resistance surveillance for the first time ([report](2026-07-17-who-eritrea-genomic-sequencing-national-health-laboratory)).
developments:
Eritrea's national health laboratory has built genomic sequencing capacity since 2024, training 15 professionals — 13 from the health ministry and two from agriculture — and applying the capability to malaria and antimicrobial-resistance surveillance for the first time nationally ([report](2026-07-17-who-eritrea-genomic-sequencing-national-health-laboratory)).

The standing platform is [DHIS2, deployed across the national health system since 2015 and run offline over the health ministry's own networks, with data entered at zone and sub-zone level and analysed centrally](2024-03-13-dhis2-eritrea-connectivity).

No coverage figure for the platform is published at any date.

The capacity behind health data is measured only historically: an assessment updated in March 2021 over 2013-2018 data found [51 per cent of the 54 health-related sustainable development indicators had a data point in the preceding five years](2021-03-15-who-score-eritrea-assessment). Nothing more recent is held.
qualifier: HIS in the ministry's sector plan and on DHIS2; reporting completeness not published

summary: The health ministry's platform runs offline within its own networks ([account](2024-03-13-dhis2-eritrea-connectivity)); no exchange standard or shared patient identifier is recorded.
developments:
The health ministry runs DHIS2 offline over its own local area networks, with decentralised data entry at zone and sub-zone level and centralised analysis ([account](2024-03-13-dhis2-eritrea-connectivity)); nothing states that it exchanges data with any system outside the ministry.

A nationally owned health-data programme was launched around the 2025 population and health survey, led by the statistics office and the health ministry, intended to produce timely disaggregated evidence accessible to government and partners ([case study](2025-11-24-unfpa-eritrea-ephs-2025-case-study)).

A survey programme is not interoperability. Nothing on the repository records a standard adopted, an exchange built or a patient identifier shared between systems.
qualifier: health information system in service; no exchange between health systems or cited absence on record

summary: The ministry rates its teacher management information systems weak and sent a delegation to learn the practice ([workshop](2025-12-16-unesco-iicba-eritrea-tmis-zambia-workshop)).
developments:
An education ministry delegation attended a regional competency enhancement workshop in Lusaka in June 2025, reported in December, to learn teacher management information system practice ([workshop](2025-12-16-unesco-iicba-eritrea-tmis-zambia-workshop)).

The education sector reform compact of September 2023 used analysis of the education management information system database to identify the barriers it addresses ([compact](2023-09-01-eritrea-2023-2027-partnership-compact)).

Both systems are described in planning documents and neither is shown exchanging data with anything else; the ministry itself rates the teacher system weak.
qualifier: EMIS and teacher system in development; no link or cited absence on record

progress: No change, a first statement of the position with nothing on exchange
summary: A vulnerability database was established in the labour ministry; nothing states it exchanges data with any other system ([results report](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022)).
developments:
United Nations support helped the labour and human welfare ministry establish a vulnerability database to collect, collate and analyse gender-segregated data on persons with disabilities, single-women-headed households and other vulnerable groups ([results report](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022)).

The report does not state that the database exchanges data with the population registers, the health information system or any payment mechanism, and a 2022 structured assessment records no system exchanging data across social insurance ([dataset](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech)).

So the repository holds one database and no exchange, which is the whole of what can be said.
qualifier: vulnerability database with no exchange stated; no cited absence

summary: A regional peer assessment records a state-owned financial system with no cash machines, cards or internet banking ([evaluation](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report)).
developments:
A regional anti-money-laundering peer assessment, adopted in July 2025 after an on-site visit in 2024, states that Eritrea's financial system is state-owned and offers simple and less sophisticated services, with no automatic teller machines, debit or credit cards, or internet banking ([evaluation](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report)).

There is therefore nothing for payments legislation to regulate, and the repository holds no payment systems act, no e-money regulation and no licensing regime.

The one instrument on the ledger is a central bank legal notice ordering cash deposits, which is currency management rather than payments law.
qualifier: cash-deposit notice and absent mobile money on record; no payment-systems law or cited absence

summary: The financial system has no cash machines, cards or internet banking, and no government-to-person payment rail is recorded ([evaluation](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report)).
developments:
Eritrea is not among the countries with live participants in, or reachable through, the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System in June 2026 ([coverage](2026-06-01-papss-payments-network-coverage-june-2026)).

The financial system it would run on has no cash machines, cards or internet banking ([evaluation](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report)).

Nothing on the repository records a government-to-person payment channel or a plan to build one.
qualifier: cash dominates per 2026 trade account; government payment channels not described

summary: A [financial-sector modernisation project remains prospective](2026-05-11-afdb-eritrea-deepen-partnership-mission), on a financial system with [no cash machines, cards or internet banking](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report).
developments:
A development bank delegation visited in April 2026 and reviewed continued dialogue on a prospective financial sector modernisation project, with discussions covering financial-sector modernisation and data systems ([mission](2026-05-11-afdb-eritrea-deepen-partnership-mission)). The project is prospective, not approved.

The system it would modernise has no cash machines, debit or credit cards, or internet banking ([evaluation](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report)).

The position was searched again: a [sector account of the country's fintech position in March 2026 describes wallets linked to the state operator as an emerging entry point still limited in functionality, records online banking, cash machines and mobile financial applications as largely absent, and puts total online commerce at under US$10m a year](2026-03-30-eritreas-fintech-ecosystem-2026-financial-inclusion).
qualifier: operator-linked wallets described as emerging and limited, trade account only; no licensed mobile-money operator

summary: A development bank mission in April 2026 reopened dialogue on a prospective financial-sector modernisation project ([mission](2026-05-11-afdb-eritrea-deepen-partnership-mission)).
developments:
A development bank delegation led by its East Africa director general met the senior adviser to the president and the finance minister in April 2026, with line-ministry discussions covering financial-sector modernisation and data systems, and both sides reviewing continued dialogue on a prospective project ([mission](2026-05-11-afdb-eritrea-deepen-partnership-mission)).

The standing umbrella instrument is the 2022-2026 cooperation framework with the United Nations development system, which seeks to expand access to health coverage, education, social protection, energy and digital connectivity ([framework](2021-01-01-un-eritrea-sustainable-development-cooperation-framework-2022-2026)).

That framework expires in 2026 and the repository holds no successor.

progress: No change, a first statement of the position with no citizen-facing service on the repository
summary: The one government digital system inaugurated in the window is an internal customs platform ([account](2026-01-08-undp-eritrea-asycuda-world-digital-customs)).
developments:
Eritrea inaugurated a customs platform in January 2026, replacing legacy software operational since 2007, with full source-code transfer to the government, an intranet architecture connecting all customs stations independent of continuous internet access, solar-powered servers and a ten-month capacity-building programme ([account](2026-01-08-undp-eritrea-asycuda-world-digital-customs)). It serves customs officials, not the public.

The standing external measurement is the 2024 United Nations e-government survey ([technical appendix](2024-10-30-un-egovernment-survey-2024-technical-appendix)); its country-level index values for Eritrea are not in the text held, so the repository names the measurement without carrying its numbers.

No online government service a citizen could use is recorded anywhere on the repository.
qualifier: 2022 govtech dataset records no online public service portal; no citizen-facing service since

progress: No change, a first statement of the position and the channel is one operator's, not government's
summary: The state telecommunications provider runs a web complaint form for internet faults; no whole-of-government channel exists ([complaint hub](2026-08-31-eritel-internet-complaint-hub)).
developments:
The sole state telecommunications provider operates a live web form for internet-connectivity, website-access and web-application problems, with telephone and email alternatives ([complaint hub](2026-08-31-eritel-internet-complaint-hub)). It is the clearest operational digital feedback channel located, and it is narrowly sector-specific.

Nothing on the repository records a government complaint portal, a service-standards charter or a published response record, and there is no freedom of information law under which an unanswered complaint could be pursued ([review contribution](2026-01-01-unesco-upr46-eritrea-freedom-of-information)).

The repository holds no volume of complaints made or resolved.
qualifier: Only the state telecom operator's customer complaint form, not a channel for feedback to government (CC)

summary: Planned regional cable and data-infrastructure projects carried no commitment to serve Asmara in 2021 ([overview](2021-06-21-world-bank-overview-digital-development-horn-of-africa-eritrea)).
developments:
A regional digital development overview records that planned submarine and festoon cable and regional data-infrastructure projects lack a commitment to serve the region as a whole, including Asmara ([overview](2021-06-21-world-bank-overview-digital-development-horn-of-africa-eritrea)).

The repository holds no cable landing and no cross-border interconnection for the country.
qualifier: no cable landing; planned regional projects carry no commitment to serve Asmara

progress: No change, no affordability figure held
summary: No affordability ratio is held; the operator's published terms put a fixed line at a one-time 882 nakfa ([terms](2025-01-01-eritel-apply-for-services)).
developments:
No entry-level broadband price for the country is held at any date, so no affordability ratio can be stated and no direction is given.

The operator's own published terms are the only prices the repository holds directly: [a fixed telephone line costs a one-time payment of 882 nakfa on top of a written request, an application form and a copy of the identity card](2025-01-01-eritel-apply-for-services), and [prepaid mobile recharge is sold in denominations of 110 and 330 nakfa, recharged by a dialled code](2025-01-01-eritel-faqs). No tariff per minute or per gigabyte is published.

progress: No change, a first statement of the position and it records one regional activity, not a scheme
summary: One regional training reached 108 government employees in computer technology and networking, 63 of them women ([report](2025-11-01-shabait-anseba-vocational-training-government-employees)).
developments:
A workers' confederation branch provided vocational training in computer technology and computer networking to 108 government employees and force members, 63 of them women, reported in November 2025 ([report](2025-11-01-shabait-anseba-vocational-training-government-employees)).

It is the clearest documented evidence that digital training reaching government employees exists, and it is a regional activity rather than a permanent nationwide scheme; no standing instrument was located at the probe date. The 2005 education ICT policy requires training only for education-sector staff ([policy](2005-07-01-eritrea-national-policy-ict-in-education)).

The repository holds one course and no measure of civil-service digital skills.

summary: The engineering college showed 26 research papers and 29 demonstrations from 1,694 students, 39% of them women ([report](2026-05-08-shabait-mai-nefhi-engineering-day)).
developments:
Mai Nefhi College of Engineering and Technology held its engineering day in May 2026 under the theme of innovation for national development, showing 26 research papers and engineering solutions, 32 illustrations and 29 engineering demonstrations, from a college of 1,694 students of whom 39% are women, across five-year degree and three-year diploma programmes ([report](2026-05-08-shabait-mai-nefhi-engineering-day)).

The qualifications themselves are longstanding: the institute of technology, established in 2004 and restructured into autonomous colleges in 2018, offers computer engineering degrees and computer, communication and electrical technology diplomas ([account](2019-07-17-shabait-eit-12th-commencement)).

The repository holds student numbers and event output, and no graduate count or employment destination.
qualifier: on the country's reported figure via uis-stem-graduates

progress: No change, a first statement of the position and the only such system on the repository
summary: One agricultural expert system, described by the ministry as part of artificial intelligence, gives farmers guidance when extension workers are unavailable ([account](2021-01-16-shabait-agricultural-strategic-information-system-eritrea-ai)).
developments:
The agriculture ministry's strategic information system division, established in 2019, includes an agricultural expert system that the ministry itself describes as part of artificial intelligence, used to give farmers guidance when extension workers are unavailable ([account](2021-01-16-shabait-agricultural-strategic-information-system-eritrea-ai)).

It is the only documented instance of a named artificial-intelligence component inside an Eritrean sectoral management information system, and the account is the ministry's own with nothing testing its use or effect.

The repository holds no later statement of whether the system still runs.
qualifier: agriculture ministry's own description of an expert system as AI, 2021 state media

progress: No change, a first statement of the position and the only response on the record is external
summary: AI-generated war imagery circulated widely and was documented by external fact-checking ([fact check](2026-04-02-afp-factcheck-ai-warfare-ethiopia-eritrea)).
developments:
A fact-checking service documented AI-generated images and videos through 2026 — tanks entering Assab, the president pursued by a foreign army chief, troops surrendering — circulating from both pro-Ethiopian and pro-Eritrean accounts, drawing large engagement and inflaming war narratives ([fact check](2026-04-02-afp-factcheck-ai-warfare-ethiopia-eritrea)).

The response on the record is entirely external. Eritrea has no artificial-intelligence law, no national strategy and no regulator ([review](2026-06-08-levellers-ai-regulation-eritrea)), and no data-protection authority to which a person depicted could complain ([redetermination](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection)).

There is no domestic mechanism of any kind on the repository for identifying, labelling or removing synthetic media.
qualifier: only external fact-checking on record; no cited absence of rule or authority

progress: No change, a first statement of the position and one hub on the repository
summary: One technology hub is documented: a youth union training centre teaching electronics, programming and robotics ([account](2025-04-09-shabait-innovation-hub-nueys-youth-entrepreneurship)).
developments:
The Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Hub, established in 2023 by the national union of Eritrean youth and students, runs three levels of six-month technical training in electronics, Python, Scratch, robotics and soldering, primarily for students in grades 9 to 11 ([account](2025-04-09-shabait-innovation-hub-nueys-youth-entrepreneurship)).

It is the clearest documented operating technology hub in Eritrea, and it is a training centre rather than an incubator: nothing on the repository records a company founded through it, investment placed or a product taken to market.

No commercial or university-attached hub is recorded anywhere.
qualifier: one youth-union hub running training courses; no incubation cohorts on record

summary: No assessment of ICT at sub-national government offices is held; a 2002 education sector note lists such a chapter the captured text does not reach ([sector note](2002-07-08-worldbank-eritrea-education-training-sector-note)).
developments:
The only candidate is a 2002 World Bank education and training sector note whose contents list a chapter on information and communication technology infrastructure ([sector note](2002-07-08-worldbank-eritrea-education-training-sector-note)); the captured text does not reach it, so no figure for sub-national offices is held.

Nothing later on the repository measures ICT at sub-national government offices, so neither a level nor a direction can be stated.
qualifier: only source does not reach its ICT chapter

summary: Technical workshops in Asmara brought government, academic, private-sector and non-governmental participants into planning for the first time on the repository ([workshops](2026-08-25-eurac-nbs4water-geodesign-asmara)).
developments:
A water project held two rounds of geodesign workshops in Asmara in July 2026 with more than twenty government, academic, private-sector and non-governmental participants, using a geodesign platform with high-resolution hydrological modelling for two catchments, alongside a modelling training session for Eritrean technical experts ([workshops](2026-08-25-eurac-nbs4water-geodesign-asmara)).

Eritrea completed its first national development plan, described as drafted through participatory, gender-responsive and results-based methods with cross-ministerial and stakeholder consultation ([annual report](2026-06-01-undp-eritrea-annual-report-2025-ndp)).

Both accounts are the conveners' own descriptions of process, not independent evidence of influence, and they sit against a surveillance system a UN commission found was used to instil fear ([findings](2015-06-05-un-coi-eritrea-detailed-findings-chapter-vi)).
qualifier: Ad hoc workshops with non-governmental participants; no required or standing consultation with published responses

progress: No change, a first measurement with no earlier figure behind it
summary: About [27% of the population uses the internet, with fixed broadband subscriptions effectively negligible](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile).
developments:
A country profile carries the 2023 international telecommunication union figures: [85% of the population covered by a mobile-cellular network, 35% by at least third-generation service and 0% by at least fourth-generation, with fixed broadband subscriptions effectively negligible](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile), and puts [internet use at about 27% of the population on a separate estimate](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile).

Coverage and use are two different numbers here and the gap between them is the finding. [Five-sixths of the population live inside a mobile-cellular signal, about a third inside one carrying third-generation data and none inside fourth-generation](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile), while about a quarter use the internet at all. With [no public submarine cable landing station, the operator's internet connectivity relies on geostationary satellite links](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile), which is the ceiling under all three.

These are first figures for this repository with nothing earlier behind them, so no direction can be stated.
qualifier: on the compiler's modelled estimate (itu-sdg-17-8-1-internet-use), no survey since 2015

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: There is [no public national cybersecurity strategy](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile); the one recorded incident is a government announcement.
developments:
A country profile records that [Eritrea has no public national cybersecurity strategy](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile).

The single incident on record is the state's own account of it: in [May 2024 the government publicly announced that the country's internet system had been hit by what it called a massive cyberattack, repelled without service interruption](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile). No incident detail, attribution, response body or computer emergency response team is named, and nothing independent corroborates either the attack or its repulse.

That is the whole of what this repository holds on cybersecurity for the country - one stated absence and one unverifiable claim.
qualifier: 2025 profile records no public strategy; no CERT or response body on record

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The sector rests on a [1998 communications proclamation and its regulations](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile); the only sectoral policy named is [for education](2026-09-02-eritrea-technology-education-profile).
developments:
The repository holds no national digital or ICT strategy for this country. What it holds instead is the sector's legal furniture, listed in a country profile and not held as text: [Communications Proclamation 102 of 1998, which set the legal basis for communications, the Regulations on Telecommunications Networks and Services issued as Legal Notice 43 of 1998, and a 2003 proclamation establishing the state telecommunications corporation](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile).

The one sector-specific policy named anywhere is [a National Policy for ICT in Education setting goals for connectivity, ministry systems, staff training and school use of technology](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile). The [2018-2022 National Education Sector Plan carries it forward, aiming at technology infrastructure and e-learning options, on the back of an ICT in education initiative the ministry launched in January 2005](2026-09-02-eritrea-technology-education-profile).

The sector plan states its own result: [incorporating technology in education remains difficult for want of facilities, equipment and teacher training](2026-09-02-eritrea-technology-education-profile). Neither the policy nor the plan is held as a document, and the profile carrying them is a legacy platform its publisher states is no longer updated.
qualifier: 1998 communications law known only through a profile; no ICT or telecoms policy or strategy on record

summary: Bids for an [integrated tax administration system were invited in September 2023](2023-09-07-eritrea-eritas-spn-afdb); the financier [rated implementation satisfactory in June 2026](2026-06-15-afdb-estap-eritas-implementation-progress-report).
developments:
2023-09-07 - the finance ministry [invited sealed bids for the supply, installation and configuration of an integrated tax administration system with its hardware and IT equipment, under a development bank governance-sector project](2023-09-07-eritrea-eritas-spn-afdb).

The scope is a full replacement, not an add-on: [implementation services with training, change management and quality assurance; cleaning, validation and migration of legacy data from the current system; deployment from a main production site to other locations in the capital and to every inland revenue office in the zobas; data replication and business continuity for disaster recovery; and support under a service level agreement](2023-09-07-eritrea-eritas-spn-afdb).

The tender proceeded: the financier's June 2026 supervision report records [software licences, hardware and installation complete and implementation rated satisfactory](2026-06-15-afdb-estap-eritas-implementation-progress-report). No go-live date is published.
qualifier: integrated tax system procured 2023, not live; no e-filing or e-payment on record

summary: The [2025 vital statistics return leaves registration completeness blank](2025-01-01-eritrea-2025-vital-statistics-metadata-questionnaire); the only structural account of the system is from 2002.
developments:
The country's [return to the United Nations vital statistics questionnaire for reporting year 2025 leaves the completeness fields for birth and death registration blank](2025-01-01-eritrea-2025-vital-statistics-metadata-questionnaire), so no registration completeness estimate is reported at all - which is itself the most current statement the repository has.

The only description of the system's shape is twenty-four years old and is stated as such: [birth registration then ran under a transitional civil code in eight named urban areas only and not in rural areas, was optional rather than obligatory even there, was kept for administrative purposes with no statistical data retained, and the urban offices did not know their own annual registered births](2002-10-21-eritrea-demographic-profile-birth-registration). The same account records that [no proper registration system or population census had been conducted before or since independence in 1991](2002-10-21-eritrea-demographic-profile-birth-registration).

Nothing between those two dates is held, so whether the 2002 position still describes the system cannot be stated - only that nobody has reported a completeness figure since.

What is known about document practice comes from outside: a foreign ministry's [country of origin report of December 2023 describes how passports and civil documents are applied for, including from abroad](2023-12-31-netherlands-eritrea-country-origin-information-report). No national registration figures are published.
qualifier: registration partial with no figures; whether digital or paper not stated

progress: No change, a first measurement with no earlier figure behind it
summary: More than [70% of Eritreans are estimated to remain unbanked](2026-03-30-eritreas-fintech-ecosystem-2026-financial-inclusion), with cash dominating economic activity.
developments:
A trade account of the country's position in 2026 estimates that [more than 70% of Eritreans remain unbanked, on a highly centralised financial system of a small number of state-owned banks, one of which provides the majority of retail banking](2026-03-30-eritreas-fintech-ecosystem-2026-financial-inclusion). It links that structure to [limited competition, minimal innovation and heavy reliance on manual processes, with online banking, cash machines and mobile financial applications largely absent so cash continues to dominate](2026-03-30-eritreas-fintech-ecosystem-2026-financial-inclusion).

The digital economy it would serve is correspondingly small: [total online commerce is estimated at under US$10m a year, and mobile penetration was just under 60% of population in 2022, ranked 191st of 209 economies](2026-03-30-eritreas-fintech-ecosystem-2026-financial-inclusion).

These are a trade publication's estimates, not a central bank or survey series, and no official financial inclusion measurement for the country is held at any date. The figure is reported for what it is.

progress: No change, a first stated position with no earlier account behind it
summary: The identity card is [required to open a telephone line](2025-01-01-eritel-apply-for-services) - the one documented use of it by another system.
developments:
With [no foundational digital identity system in service](2025-07-26 Eritrea's population digital identity - challenges ahead), there is no digital credential for another system to consume. What the repository can show is the paper card being used as a precondition: the state operator requires, for a fixed telephone line, [a written request with address and contact number, a completed application form, a copy of the identity card and a one-time payment of 882 nakfa](2025-01-01-eritel-apply-for-services).

That is a documentary check at a counter, not an authentication against a register, and it runs the wrong way round from what this indicator asks: the card gates access to a service rather than a service verifying against an identity system. It is the only such link the repository holds.

The other established dependency is internal to the state: [a national identity document is required before an Eritrean passport can be issued](2026-03-02-uk-gov-eritrea-knowledge-base-profile).
qualifier: ID card copy required for a telephone line, on the operator's own terms; no verification service

summary: No national digital transformation strategy is held. What exists is sectoral: a policy for [technology in education](2026-09-02-eritrea-technology-education-profile) and a geospatial framework action plan.
developments:
The repository holds two sectoral instruments touching digital questions and no overarching one. The first is the policy for [technology in education](2026-09-02-eritrea-technology-education-profile), which governs one sector. The second is a [domesticated geospatial information framework action plan filed in April 2026](2026-04-06-uneca-eritrea-domesticated-igif-action-plan), which concerns one class of data.

Against that, the telecommunications union's own survey of national plans [records the country as having no adopted broadband strategy](2019-01-01-itu-broadband-strategies-policies-plans-2019). A country with a sector policy for schools, an action plan for maps and nothing for the network they both run on has no strategy in the sense this indicator asks about, and nothing on the repository records one being drafted.
qualifier: only a sectoral ICT-in-education policy on record, via a secondary profile; no national digital strategy

summary: The telecommunications union's own survey of national plans [records the country as having none](2019-01-01-itu-broadband-strategies-policies-plans-2019). Nothing later on the repository records one being adopted.
developments:
The absence is documented rather than merely unfound. The telecommunications union's survey of broadband strategies, policies and plans [carries the country in its table with no plan against it](2019-01-01-itu-broadband-strategies-policies-plans-2019); neighbouring entries in the same table carry theirs, so the reading is unambiguous.

What governs the sector instead is the [communications proclamation of 1998](1998-03-02-eritrea-communications-proclamation-102), which makes the ministry's communications department sole regulator and sets the development of national communications capability as an objective without setting a target for it. Nothing published since names a broadband target, a coverage obligation or a date.
qualifier: no adopted broadband plan on the telecommunications union's 2019 country table

summary: No storage or cloud strategy is held. The nearest thing to a stated position is the state operator's own [private cloud service](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services), hosted in its own data centres.
developments:
Nothing on the repository states where government data should be held, on whose equipment, or under what terms. The one document that describes domestic hosting at all is a commercial one: the state operator's [private cloud service page](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services), which offers subscription storage hosted entirely in the operator's own facilities.

That makes domestic hosting the practical default without anyone having chosen it as a policy. No public body's hosting arrangement is published, no procurement rule addresses it, and [no local data-storage requirement is recorded](2022-01-01-uneca-dtri-eritrea-digital-trade-regulatory-country-profile).
qualifier: No hosting or cloud policy on record; the state operator's commercial private cloud is a service, not a policy

summary: No localisation or residency rule is held. Domestic hosting happens anyway, because the [only provider-hosted cloud on the repository](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services) is the state operator's own.
developments:
No instrument states where public or personal data may be held. There is no hosting duty on public bodies, no rule on transfers out and no authority that could grant or refuse one, the [data-protection law itself being absent](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection).

What produces localisation in practice is the shape of the market rather than a rule. The state operator's [private cloud](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services) is hosted in its own data centres, and no foreign provider is recorded serving the country. Data stays where it is because there is nowhere else for it to go, which is not the same position as a country that has chosen it.
qualifier: No localisation or residency rule; hosting at home is practice, not a legal duty

summary: No open data policy or licence is held. Government data reaches the public as survey reports, not as datasets.
developments:
Nothing on the repository names an open data policy or a licence under which government data is released; a 2022 dataset records only [a basic open data portal](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech). The [national population and health survey of 2025](2025-09-01-unfpa-eritrea-ephs-2025-data-for-development) is the largest data-collection exercise in fifteen years, and its output was a report scheduled for the following year rather than a published dataset.

The pattern holds across the repository: the [geospatial capacity programme](2026-03-01-uneca-eritrea-geospatial-capacity-workshop) produces trained analysts and classified imagery for ministry use, and nothing produced under it is published. Data here is produced for the state's own use, and the question of releasing it has not been put.
qualifier: A basic portal recorded in 2022 with no policy or licence behind it

summary: No data-protection law and no authority. A [legal survey](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection) and a [regional policy matrix](2025-09-01-hoai-digital-policy-matrix-update-data-protection-nascent) agree that neither exists.
developments:
There is nothing to supervise and no one to supervise it. A [legal survey](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection) records no data-protection statute, and a [regional policy matrix](2025-09-01-hoai-digital-policy-matrix-update-data-protection-nascent) places the country at the nascent end of its own scale. A [digital trade regulatory profile](2022-01-01-uneca-dtri-eritrea-digital-trade-regulatory-country-profile) reaches the same finding from a different direction.

The absence has consequences elsewhere on this ledger. Without an authority there is no route for a complaint about personal data, no body that could authorise a transfer out of the country, and nothing that could act on synthetic or manipulated media. Each of those reads as a separate gap; all of them are this one.
qualifier: No law and so no authority provided for; reconfirmed August 2026

summary: The [sole non-signatory](2026-07-01-tralac-afcfta-legal-texts-policy-documents) to the continental trade agreement, and outside the coverage of the regional body's [digital integration programme](2026-01-26-igad-eardip-programme-page-member-states).
developments:
Of 55 member states of the continental union, [only this one has yet to sign](2026-07-01-tralac-afcfta-legal-texts-policy-documents) the consolidated text of the free trade agreement, with 49 having signed and deposited ratification instruments. That agreement covers digital trade among its areas.

Membership of the regional body has not produced participation either. The body's digital integration programme, which covers data governance and cross-border data flows, [states its coverage as seven named member states](2026-01-26-igad-eardip-programme-page-member-states) and does not include this one.
qualifier: sole AfCFTA non-signatory at July 2026; outside the regional digital integration programme

summary: Nothing to harmonise with. The country has [not signed the continental trade agreement](2026-07-01-tralac-afcfta-legal-texts-policy-documents) and is [outside the regional digital programme](2026-01-26-igad-eardip-programme-page-member-states).
developments:
Harmonisation runs through the two frameworks the country stands outside. The continental free trade agreement, whose scope includes digital trade, [has not been signed here](2026-07-01-tralac-afcfta-legal-texts-policy-documents). The regional body's digital integration programme, which works on harmonised policies for data governance, cybersecurity and data protection, [names seven participating states and not this one](2026-01-26-igad-eardip-programme-page-member-states).

There is also little on the domestic side to bring into line. No data-protection law, [no electronic-signature legislation](2022-01-01-uneca-dtri-eritrea-digital-trade-regulatory-country-profile) and no cybersecurity strategy exist to be harmonised with anything.
qualifier: Sole non-signatory to the continental trade agreement; outside the regional digital programme; no cyberlaw to harmonise

summary: No transfer rule, because there is no data-protection law to carry one, and [no participation](2026-07-01-tralac-afcfta-legal-texts-policy-documents) in the framework that would supply one.
developments:
Cross-border transfer is governed by nothing. There is [no data-protection statute](2026-08-01-lawlab-africa-eritrea-data-protection) under which a transfer rule could sit, no authority that could authorise or refuse one, and no adequacy or localisation position of any kind.

Nor is one arriving from outside. The continental agreement whose scope includes digital trade [has not been signed](2026-07-01-tralac-afcfta-legal-texts-policy-documents), and the regional programme drafting harmonised rules [does not cover the country](2026-01-26-igad-eardip-programme-page-member-states). The financial system shows what that isolation looks like in practice: the regional peer assessment records a sector [less integrated with the global financial system](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report), with none of the instruments that would move data across a border in the first place.
qualifier: Nothing states where personal data may be held or how it may leave

summary: A [standards institution since 1995](1995-09-20-proclamation-75-eritrean-standards-institution) and a [regulator charged with setting technical standards](1998-03-02-eritrea-communications-proclamation-102). Neither has published an interoperability standard.
developments:
The institutional basis exists twice over. The [standards institution was constituted in 1995](1995-09-20-proclamation-75-eritrean-standards-institution), and the [communications proclamation of 1998](1998-03-02-eritrea-communications-proclamation-102) makes the ministry's communications department sole sector regulator and sets the establishment of technical standards among its objectives.

What neither has produced is a published standard for how government systems exchange data. Nothing on the repository names an interoperability framework, a data dictionary or a common identifier convention, and the systems that do exist run separately: customs on its own platform, tax on another, health on a third, with no exchange layer between them.
qualifier: standards body since 1995 with no digital standard recorded; no cited absence of interoperability standards

summary: No domestic budget line and no institution to raise one. The [investment centre is dormant and the investment law effectively suspended](2025-01-01-us-state-dept-2025-investment-climate-statement-eritrea).
developments:
The external country assessment establishes the position directly: [the investment centre created in 1998 is dormant and the 1994 investment law is effectively suspended](2025-01-01-us-state-dept-2025-investment-climate-statement-eritrea), with what non-state finance arrives negotiated case by case rather than through any standing institution.

No published budget names digital transformation as a line, and no revenue instrument is earmarked to it. What financing the repository can see is external and project-shaped: the [tax administration system](2026-06-15-afdb-estap-eritas-implementation-progress-report) and the [education programme grants](2024-04-19-gpe-eri-001-eritrea-emis-system-transformation-grant) are both financed from outside, and both would stop with their grants.
qualifier: no budget document read; external assessment covers investment institutions, not a digital budget line

summary: No blended-finance or private-investment route. The [investment centre is dormant, the investment law suspended](2025-01-01-us-state-dept-2025-investment-climate-statement-eritrea), and deals are negotiated case by case.
developments:
The external country assessment is unambiguous about the machinery: [the investment centre is dormant and the investment law effectively suspended](2025-01-01-us-state-dept-2025-investment-climate-statement-eritrea), leaving no institution through which private or blended finance could be mobilised for anything, digital or otherwise.

The one active engagement on the repository runs the other way, from a public financier rather than a private one: a [bank mission to deepen the partnership](2026-05-11-afdb-eritrea-deepen-partnership-mission) and an [interim country strategy naming payment systems a priority to 2027](2025-11-01-afdb-eritrea-interim-country-strategy-paper-2025-2027). Neither mobilises non-state money; both propose to build the frameworks that would have to exist before any could be mobilised.
qualifier: no private digital commitment starting 2024–2026 on record

summary: None. The exchange tracker [records no active exchange point and no listing in the peering database](2026-01-01-isoc-pulse-ixp-tracker-eritrea).
developments:
The tracker states it directly: [there are no active internet exchange points in the country and none listed in the peering database](2026-01-01-isoc-pulse-ixp-tracker-eritrea). The tracker notes that networks using an exchange point rather than direct transit reduce their reliance on international traffic.
