A [long-form policy piece argues that domestic traffic should not needlessly leave the country](2026-08-10-mesobjournal-eritrea-digital-sovereignty); no government document proposes an exchange. Nothing records a peering arrangement being negotiated or an exchange being constituted.
qualifier: Exchange tracker records none active; August diaspora proposal has no government adoption

summary: One provider, and it is the state operator. Its [private cloud is hosted entirely in its own data centres](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services); no other facility is named on the repository.
developments:
The repository now holds primary evidence that domestic hosting capacity exists, which it did not before. The state operator's [private cloud service](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services) is offered in three subscription tiers and hosted entirely in the operator's own facilities.

What it does not hold is any measure of that capacity. No aggregate figure, facility count, floor area, power draw or location is published for the country by anyone, and no second provider appears anywhere. A [long-form policy piece argues that critical state information and nationally important services should be capable of being hosted domestically](2026-08-10-mesobjournal-eritrea-digital-sovereignty), which is an argument rather than a measure.
qualifier: no multi-tenant data centre in service in Corpus's dataset of the 54

summary: The only national provider is the state operator, whose [private cloud runs in its own data centres](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services). No capacity figure is published at any date.
developments:
National capacity and total capacity are the same number here, because the state operator is the only provider on the repository. Its [private cloud](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services) offers storage tiers of 100, 250 and 500 gigabytes for 20, 50 and 100 users, hosted in its own facilities.

Those are subscription sizes rather than a statement of the estate behind them, and nothing published says how large that estate is, where it sits or how it is powered. The [grid it draws on delivers 52 MW reliably against 74.3 MW of demand](2026-02-01-afdb-energy-integrated-project-appraisal-grid-reliability), which is the practical ceiling on how much of anything can be hosted here.

summary: The only published recovery commitment is the state operator's: a [six-day recovery objective on a 90 per cent uptime service level](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services).
developments:
No government backup arrangement is published for any system, and no second site is named for any of them. The one figure the repository can offer comes from the commercial side: the state operator's private cloud [states a 90 per cent uptime service level and a recovery-time objective of up to six days](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services).

That is the measure of what recovery means in this market. A six-day objective is what a subscriber is promised by the country's only provider, and nothing suggests the systems the government runs itself are held to anything better. Whether the customs, tax or health systems have off-site copies at all is not stated anywhere on the repository.
qualifier: Only the state operator's commercial private cloud (six-day recovery objective) is held; no government backup site or contract on record

summary: The grid [delivers 52 MW reliably against 74.3 MW of demand](2026-02-01-afdb-energy-integrated-project-appraisal-grid-reliability). No data centre's supply arrangement or water requirement is published.
developments:
The financier's appraisal states the position: [installed capacity of 157 MW with only 52 MW reliably available against demand of 74.3 MW](2026-02-01-afdb-energy-integrated-project-appraisal-grid-reliability), renewables at 6 MW, and generation almost entirely reliant on imported diesel through ageing and breakdown-prone plant.

A grid meeting two thirds of the demand already placed on it is the constraint every hosted system in the country sits behind. Against that, no facility's supply arrangement, tariff, generator provision or water requirement is published for the [one provider-hosted cloud on the repository](2026-08-31-eritel-private-cloud-services), and the question of whether a data centre could be powered here has not been publicly put.

summary: A financier's appraisal put [52 MW of 157 MW reliably available against 74.3 MW of demand](2026-02-01-afdb-energy-integrated-project-appraisal-grid-reliability); a [twelve-centre architecture](2026-01-24-shabait-president-isaias-interview-12-minigrid-energy-plan) was stated in answer.
developments:
Two things happened in the window and neither is a megawatt. In January the head of state set out a decentralised architecture in interview: [twelve independent mini-grid power centres targeting 360 MW, each growing to 30 MW and eventually interconnected toward about 2,000 MW](2026-01-24-shabait-president-isaias-interview-12-minigrid-energy-plan), framed explicitly against the inadequacy of the existing centralised grid.

In February the financier's appraisal stated the position it is answering: [installed capacity 157 MW with 52 MW reliably available against 74.3 MW of demand](2026-02-01-afdb-energy-integrated-project-appraisal-grid-reliability), renewables at 6 MW and generation reliant on imported diesel through ageing plant. No site, cost, financier or date has been published against the twelve centres.

progress: Movement, an architecture stated and nothing sited
summary: The head of state set out [twelve mini-grid centres targeting 360 MW](2026-01-24-shabait-president-isaias-interview-12-minigrid-energy-plan), decentralised by design. No site, cost or date has been published.
developments:
The stated approach is decentralisation rather than extension of the existing network: [twelve independent mini-grid power centres, each growing to 30 MW toward a 360 MW target, to be interconnected later](2026-01-24-shabait-president-isaias-interview-12-minigrid-energy-plan). For a country where the grid reaches a minority of the population, that is the right shape of answer.

It remains an architecture. Nothing names a site, a cost, a financier or a date, and the [appraisal from a month later](2026-02-01-afdb-energy-integrated-project-appraisal-grid-reliability) describes a system still almost entirely dependent on imported diesel with renewables at 6 MW.
qualifier: on a survey figure via wdi-elc-accs-rural

summary: No audit of government hardware or software is held; the police [trained members from every station in computer, printer and network maintenance](2026-06-04-shabait-vocational-training-college-students-police) in June 2026.
developments:
No assessment of the robustness of government hardware or software is held. The education ministry's own list of challenges names [weak teacher management information systems and inadequate technological infrastructure and internet connectivity](2025-12-16-unesco-iicba-eritrea-tmis-zambia-workshop).

The nearest evidence on upkeep is maintenance training: the police force [trained members from every station in computer, printer and network maintenance](2026-06-04-shabait-vocational-training-college-students-police) in June 2026.
qualifier: police records system on the state's 2017 report only; core finance and revenue systems not described

progress: Movement, in training rather than in systems
summary: Three training programmes reached government staff in the window: [police maintenance](2026-06-04-shabait-vocational-training-college-students-police), [geospatial analysis](2026-07-13-shabait-eritrea-gis-training-gash-barka) and [records digitisation](2025-09-08-shabait-training-documentation-archives).
developments:
The capacity work is real and it is all training. The police trained members drawn from every station and headquarters in [computer maintenance, printer maintenance and networking](2026-06-04-shabait-vocational-training-college-students-police). One regional administration and the national documentation centre trained 64 local-institution employees in [document organisation, preservation and digital document management](2025-09-08-shabait-training-documentation-archives). A second region's administration and its sectoral branches took [geospatial training framed as closing gaps in the existing information system](2026-07-13-shabait-eritrea-gis-training-gash-barka).

Alongside those, a regional economic commission trained over 25 ministry staff in [geographic information systems, remote sensing and land-cover classification](2026-03-01-uneca-eritrea-geospatial-capacity-workshop). What none of it amounts to yet is a system built or maintained here rather than delivered from outside.
qualifier: training exercises only; no in-house team maintaining a system on record

summary: No exchange layer. The systems that exist run separately: [customs on its own platform](2026-01-08-undp-eritrea-asycuda-world-digital-customs) and a [vulnerability database](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022) in the welfare ministry.
developments:
Nothing on the repository names a national data exchange, a shared bus or a common identifier convention. What exists is a set of unconnected systems: the [customs platform inaugurated in January 2026](2026-01-08-undp-eritrea-asycuda-world-digital-customs), which serves officials on an intranet; the welfare ministry's [vulnerability database](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022); the tax system under construction; and the health information system.

There is one working instance of one system consuming another's output, and it is a legal duty rather than a technical connection: the anti-money-laundering proclamation requires financial institutions to [set customer identification policies](2014-09-08-eritrea-aml-cft-proclamation-175-2014-id-kyc).
qualifier: customs platform and a standalone database only; no exchange layer or cited absence

summary: The card is issued and maintained on paper. [Most holders still carry the old handwritten card](2025-11-01-us-state-dept-eritrea-civil-documents-national-id), with a long application backlog.
developments:
The standing position is set out in the external civil-documents reference: the identity card is issued by the immigration and nationality department at a fee of 100 nakfa, a plastic card with hologram and fingerprint was introduced late in 2015 for those aged 18 and over, and [very few new cards are in circulation, most people still holding the old handwritten cards, with a long backlog of applications](2025-11-01-us-state-dept-eritrea-civil-documents-national-id).

A credential most of whose holders carry a handwritten version is not maintained in the sense this indicator asks about. [The electronic card was being introduced to replace the handwritten one in 2018](2018-09-26-eritrea-national-id-card-ecoi), and that replacement is still incomplete.
qualifier: issued by the immigration department; platform, supplier and contracts not on record

summary: Authentication is a card shown at a counter. The [anti-money-laundering proclamation](2014-09-08-eritrea-aml-cft-proclamation-175-2014-id-kyc) requires financial institutions to identify customers; no electronic verification is recorded.
developments:
The only authentication duty on the repository is the anti-money-laundering proclamation's: financial institutions must [set customer identification and acceptance policies for business relationships and for cash transactions above US$10,000](2014-09-08-eritrea-aml-cft-proclamation-175-2014-id-kyc), with the central bank supervising.

That is authentication done by eye. There is no verification service, no electronic signature framework and no credential that could be checked against a register, and the [financial system it serves has no automatic teller machines, cards or internet banking](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report) to check one at. [Most cardholders carry a handwritten card](2025-11-01-us-state-dept-eritrea-civil-documents-national-id).
qualifier: no internet banking or cards per 2025 mutual evaluation; no statement on credential verification

summary: The [card is issued from age 18](2025-11-01-us-state-dept-eritrea-civil-documents-national-id); [birth registration feeds the zoba population registers, which also record the identity number](2021-01-21-swiss-sem-focus-eritrea-digital-population-registers).
developments:
There is no credential that follows a person from birth. Civil registration of births exists and is partial; the identity card is a separate document [issued from age 18 by the immigration and nationality department at a fee of 100 nakfa](2025-11-01-us-state-dept-eritrea-civil-documents-national-id).

The registers that do exist are held at zoba level, and [birth registration reaches them through the local family register](2021-01-21-swiss-sem-focus-eritrea-digital-population-registers).
qualifier: civil registration partial with no figures; link between birth records and ID not described

summary: Banks carry a [customer identification duty](2014-09-08-eritrea-aml-cft-proclamation-175-2014-id-kyc), and the card is [required before a passport is issued](2026-03-02-uk-gov-eritrea-knowledge-base-profile); no electronic check is recorded.
developments:
The clearest standing example of the national credential being used by a system other than the one that issues it is the anti-money-laundering proclamation, which requires financial institutions to [set customer identification policies for business relationships and large cash transactions](2014-09-08-eritrea-aml-cft-proclamation-175-2014-id-kyc).

Beyond that, a [national identity card is a precondition of passport issue](2026-03-02-uk-gov-eritrea-knowledge-base-profile) and [of a fixed telephone line](2025-01-01-eritel-apply-for-services), and there is [no online public service portal](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech) that could ask for it.
qualifier: no public register shown keyed on the national ID; no cited absence

summary: The tax administration system reached [67.21 per cent disbursement with software and hardware installed](2026-06-15-afdb-estap-eritas-implementation-progress-report) by June 2026, its progress rated satisfactory.
developments:
The financier's own supervision report is the most authoritative current statement of the system's standing: [software and hardware delivery and installation complete, the first release's requirements specification complete, disbursement at 67.21 per cent as of June 2026, and implementation progress rated satisfactory](2026-06-15-afdb-estap-eritas-implementation-progress-report). That is real movement on a project [put to tender in September 2023](2023-09-07-eritrea-eritas-spn-afdb).

What it does not yet show is revenue collected through it. No taxpayer register size is published at any date, no filing or payment volume is reported, and the [payment systems the money would move over are themselves named a priority for construction to 2027](2025-11-01-afdb-eritrea-interim-country-strategy-paper-2025-2027). Collection remains a counter transaction.
qualifier: tax system installed but not live; electronic payment or filing not in its stated scope

summary: Neither exists. The regional assessment records a state-owned sector with [no cards and no internet banking](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report).
developments:
The regional peer assessment, following an on-site visit in 2024, states that the financial system is state-owned and offers [simple and less sophisticated services with no automatic teller machines, debit or credit cards or internet banking](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report), and that the financial intelligence unit is not yet operational.

Business-to-business and business-to-government payment are not partially available here; the instruments they would run on do not exist. [Wallets linked to the state operator are an emerging entry point with limited functionality, and no independent fintech startups are present](2026-03-30-eritreas-fintech-ecosystem-2026-financial-inclusion). The financier's country strategy [names payment systems an explicit priority for 2025 to 2027](2025-11-01-afdb-eritrea-interim-country-strategy-paper-2025-2027), which is a statement that the work has not started.
qualifier: 2025 mutual evaluation: no internet banking or cards; procurement channel not on record

summary: The regional assessment finds the sector [less integrated with the global financial system](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report), with no cards and no internet banking to connect it.
developments:
The peer assessment adopted in July 2025 states the position plainly: a state-owned financial system offering [simple and less sophisticated services, with no automatic teller machines, debit or credit cards or internet banking, and less integrated with the global financial system](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report). Its financial intelligence unit is not yet operational.

Nothing else on the repository bears on cross-border payment. There is no correspondent arrangement named, no remittance corridor described and no regional settlement scheme the country participates in, which is consistent with its position [outside the continental trade agreement](2026-07-01-tralac-afcfta-legal-texts-policy-documents) and outside the regional digital programme.
qualifier: 2025 mutual evaluation: no cards or internet banking, system not integrated globally

summary: No payment consumer-protection rule, because there are no payment products. The only complaint route on the repository is the [state operator's internet complaint form](2026-08-31-eritel-internet-complaint-hub).
developments:
There is nothing for a payments consumer-protection regime to protect. The regional assessment records a state-owned sector with [no cards and no internet banking](2025-07-01-esaamlg-eritrea-mutual-evaluation-report). No dispute, chargeback or redress rule appears anywhere.

The one working consumer route the repository holds belongs to the telecommunications side: the state operator's [internet complaint form](2026-08-31-eritel-internet-complaint-hub), alongside its [published terms of access to services](2025-01-01-eritel-apply-for-services). Neither is a financial protection, and neither sits under a regulator with power to enforce.
qualifier: No digital financial services exist to regulate; the operator's complaint form covers internet service, not finance

summary: A [vulnerability database in the welfare ministry](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022) collecting gender-segregated data, under a [social protection policy running to 2026](2025-10-01-eritrea-fourth-periodic-report-acrwc-disability).
developments:
The register exists and its shape is described in the government's own periodic report: a [national social protection policy and strategic plan for 2022 to 2026, a disability policy revised in 2021, and accession to the disability rights convention in December 2024](2025-10-01-eritrea-fourth-periodic-report-acrwc-disability). Behind them sits the labour and welfare ministry's [vulnerability database, collecting gender-segregated data on persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022).

Nothing in the window changed its coverage, its size or its operation. The [external committee's observations of July 2026](2026-07-22-acerwc-concluding-observations-eritrea) are an assessment of the framework rather than a change to it.
qualifier: welfare ministry vulnerability database per UN report; programme use and coverage not on record

summary: The system that would hold it reached [67.21 per cent disbursement with hardware and software installed](2026-06-15-afdb-estap-eritas-implementation-progress-report). No register size is published at any date.
developments:
The taxpayer register is being built rather than counted. The financier's supervision report records [software and hardware delivered and installed, the first release's requirements specification complete, and disbursement at 67.21 per cent as of June 2026](2026-06-15-afdb-estap-eritas-implementation-progress-report), with implementation progress rated satisfactory against a project [put to tender in September 2023](2023-09-07-eritrea-eritas-spn-afdb).

What no source states is how many taxpayers are registered, at this or any earlier date, or what proportion of economic activity the register reaches. Until the first release runs there is no register to measure, and the repository carries the project's progress in place of the thing it will produce.
qualifier: legacy tax system implied; register integrity and identifiers not described

summary: A consultancy was sought in June 2026 for [analytical support to the education information system](2026-06-11-unesco-iicba-eritrea-emis-data-analytical-support-rfp).
developments:
The request for proposal is targeted work against a diagnosis the government has already made. It seeks a consultant for [analytical support to the education management information system, responding to identified weaknesses in analysis, gender disaggregation and data use, and requiring analysis of teacher deployment and attrition by gender and location, ministry workshops and a validated policy brief](2026-06-11-unesco-iicba-eritrea-emis-data-analytical-support-rfp), with a deadline in July 2026.

The ministry's own list of challenges includes [weak teacher management information systems and inadequate technological infrastructure and connectivity](2025-12-16-unesco-iicba-eritrea-tmis-zambia-workshop), set out before a teacher management workshop in June 2025.
qualifier: EMIS being strengthened with named weaknesses; no annual census publication on record

summary: The [vulnerability database](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022) is the system, under a [social protection policy running to 2026](2025-10-01-eritrea-fourth-periodic-report-acrwc-disability).
developments:
What exists is a register rather than a management system: the labour and welfare ministry's [vulnerability database, collecting gender-segregated data on persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022), under a [social protection policy and strategic plan running to 2026](2025-10-01-eritrea-fourth-periodic-report-acrwc-disability).

The [children's rights committee adopted concluding observations on the country's combined fifth and sixth reports at the end of January 2025](2025-03-05-ohchr-crc-concluding-observations-eritrea); the captured text does not reach its findings on data. Nothing in the window records a caseload figure, a payment record or an eligibility rule.
qualifier: vulnerability database is not a programme MIS; no programme system on record

summary: None. The justice ministry's own review of its year [names advancing the use of technology and describes no system](2025-01-10-eritrea-ministry-of-justice-activity-assessment).
developments:
The absence is established by the ministry itself. Its 2024 activity review and 2025 plan [names advancing the use of technology among its priority programmes and does not name or describe any court case-management or justice management information system](2025-01-10-eritrea-ministry-of-justice-activity-assessment). That is the best available statement of the sector's standing, and what it establishes is that no such system is on the record.

The law the sector applies compounds it. The children's rights committee recorded in April 2026 that [the 2015 Penal Code has not yet been enacted](2026-07-22-acerwc-concluding-observations-eritrea).
qualifier: ministry's own review names no system; not a statement that records are paper-based

progress: Movement, in the capacity behind it rather than in the system
summary: The [cadastral office dates from 1997](1997-05-19-eritrea-proclamation-95-1997-land-registration-cadastral-office). What moved was training: [land ministry staff in geospatial analysis](2026-02-28-eritrea-gis-training-asmara-unega), twice in the window.
developments:
The register itself is unchanged: a [cadastral office and land register constituted by proclamation in 1997](1997-05-19-eritrea-proclamation-95-1997-land-registration-cadastral-office), with no published statement of coverage, digitisation or parcel count at any date.

What moved is the analytical capacity around it. A four-week workshop trained over 25 [land, water and environment ministry staff in geographic information systems, remote sensing, land use and land cover classification and watershed analysis](2026-03-01-uneca-eritrea-geospatial-capacity-workshop), the second phase of a partnership with a regional economic commission. A [parallel course reached experts from five ministries plus the cartographic centre and regional administrations](2026-02-28-eritrea-gis-training-asmara-unega), and a [third extended it to a region in July](2026-07-13-shabait-eritrea-gis-training-gash-barka).
qualifier: cadastral office and GIS training only; no land information system on record

progress: Movement, in training rather than in records
summary: Two regional administrations took records training in the window: [64 local-institution employees in document management](2025-09-08-shabait-training-documentation-archives), then [a second region on geospatial systems](2026-07-13-shabait-eritrea-gis-training-gash-barka).
developments:
One regional administration, with the national research and documentation centre, trained 64 employees of local institutions in [document organisation, preservation, evaluation and digital document management](2025-09-08-shabait-training-documentation-archives) in September 2025. In July 2026 a second region's administration and its sectoral branches took [geospatial training framed as addressing gaps in the existing information system and improving documentation practices](2026-07-13-shabait-eritrea-gis-training-gash-barka).

Both are capacity-building rather than an operating digitised-records system. Nothing records a local register being converted.
qualifier: records training only; no records system approved or in service

summary: A [smartphone application for adverse-event reporting](2025-10-15-who-vigimobile-eritrea-workshop) was introduced to over 60 national and zonal staff, replacing paper reporting.
developments:
The workshop of October 2025 introduced [a smartphone application for reporting adverse events following immunisation and adverse drug reactions, to over 60 participants including national and zonal focal points, regulatory officers and technology specialists, framed explicitly as the transition from paper-based to digital reporting](2025-10-15-who-vigimobile-eritrea-workshop). Zonal focal points are the level at which rural clinics report, which is what makes this reach beyond the capital.

An independent long-form account reports the [introduction of a digital health policy and a health technology strategic plan for 2026 to 2030](2026-05-16-redseabeacon-eritrea-quiet-revolution-health-care); no health ministry or health agency source corroborates it, so it is carried as a claim rather than as a fact. The [national DHIS2 platform, run offline over the ministry's own networks](2024-03-13-dhis2-eritrea-connectivity), is unchanged on the record.
qualifier: focal points trained on an adverse-event reporting app, WHO 2025

summary: No rural school is recorded as digitised; [education reform grants target zobas with nomadic and remote rural communities](2024-04-19-gpe-eri-001-eritrea-emis-system-transformation-grant).
developments:
Nothing on the repository records a rural school digitised, connected or equipped. The 2018-2022 education sector plan names [insufficient electricity and telecommunications coverage as the most pressing obstacle to technology in rural schools, and plans solar power systems for them](2026-09-02-eritrea-technology-education-profile).

What no source supplies is a count of schools with equipment or a connection, at any level, rural or otherwise. The [grants financing the work](2024-04-19-gpe-eri-001-eritrea-emis-system-transformation-grant) are directed at foundational learning and the information system in zobas with nomadic and remote rural communities rather than at school equipment.
qualifier: ICT-in-education initiative and connectivity goals on a secondary profile; sector plan cites missing facilities

summary: Population registers are held at sub-national level and [described as digital in one external report](2021-01-21-swiss-sem-focus-eritrea-digital-population-registers); nothing states their coverage or reach.
developments:
Sub-national population registers exist and one external report [describes them as digital](2021-01-21-swiss-sem-focus-eritrea-digital-population-registers), which is the strongest statement the repository holds. What it does not hold is any account of how far down that reaches: no sub-region is named, no coverage figure is given, and [birth registration itself is partial](2025-01-01-eritrea-2025-vital-statistics-metadata-questionnaire).

The [children's rights committee's observations of July 2026](2026-07-22-acerwc-eritrea-concluding-observations-crvs) are the most recent external assessment of civil registration.
qualifier: digital zoba-level registers per a 2021 foreign-government report; share of offices not published

progress: Movement, in maintenance skills rather than in systems
summary: The police trained members from [every station in the country in computer, printer and network maintenance](2026-06-04-shabait-vocational-training-college-students-police) in June 2026.
developments:
The training reached beyond the capital by design: members drawn from [all police stations across the country and from headquarters, in computer maintenance, printer maintenance and computer networking](2026-06-04-shabait-vocational-training-college-students-police). Stations are evidently expected to keep equipment and network functions working without a contractor.

What the repository does not establish is that record capture is live at station level. The state's own national human rights report records the force having [established police centres in 53 sub-regions and 34 further stations in remote areas, with a computerised system managing crime records, vehicle registration, traffic violations and personnel](2017-03-28-eritrea-achpr-initial-national-report) — but does not link that system to the remote stations. Training people to maintain equipment is not the same as showing the system reaches them.
qualifier: central computerised system on the state's own 2017 report; not linked to any station

summary: One deployment, in agriculture: an [expert system for agricultural strategic information](2021-01-16-shabait-agricultural-strategic-information-system-eritrea-ai). No administrative use is recorded and [no policy governs it](2026-06-08-levellers-ai-regulation-eritrea).
developments:
The single instance on the repository is sectoral and five years old: an [agricultural expert system](2021-01-16-shabait-agricultural-strategic-information-system-eritrea-ai) reported in 2021. Nothing records a model used in administration — no case triage, no register matching, no document processing in any ministry.

The governing position is empty in both directions. A [legal-status review of June 2026 records that neither an artificial intelligence law nor a strategy exists](2026-06-08-levellers-ai-regulation-eritrea). Where AI appears in public life it is as training: an institute reports [about 50 graduates in 2026 from new introductory courses, some producing animation videos for children](2026-07-21-shabait-polytech-ai-and-the-future).
qualifier: only AI on record is the agriculture ministry's farmer-facing expert system, read under sectoral systems

summary: The [1998 proclamation](1998-03-02-eritrea-communications-proclamation-102) makes developing national communications capability an objective. Twenty-eight years on, no manufacturer or licensed supplier is named on the repository.
developments:
The legal basis is the founding sector law: the [communications proclamation makes the ministry's communications department sole regulator over telecommunications, broadcasting and post, and sets the establishment of technical standards and the development of the country's communications capabilities, industries and skills among its objectives](1998-03-02-eritrea-communications-proclamation-102), through operator licensing, equipment supplier and installer permits and a rural telecommunications fund.

What has been produced under it is software rather than hardware, and small: a developer group publishing [Tigrinya-language educational applications](2026-08-15-eritrea-shambko-apps-group-local-language-education) and a [virtual-reality rendering of national heritage](2026-09-07-shabait-eritrea-afro-verse-virtual-reality-heritage). No manufacturer, assembler or licensed equipment supplier appears anywhere on the repository.

summary: No population measure exists. What the repository counts is people who paid or were posted: [civil servants](2025-11-01-shabait-anseba-vocational-training-government-employees) and [students of a technology institute](2026-07-21-shabait-polytech-ai-and-the-future).
developments:
Nothing on the repository measures digital skill in the population — no survey, no index entry, no schooling indicator. What it holds instead are two channels that reach particular groups. Government employees receive [vocational training in one region](2025-11-01-shabait-anseba-vocational-training-government-employees), and the civil service has been the main route to skills throughout.

Outside it, a private technology institute with four branches across two cities [graduates roughly 700 young people a year from its computer technology, electrical and electronic and audio-visual departments](2026-07-21-shabait-polytech-ai-and-the-future). Both are real; neither is a population. With [mobile connections the only published penetration figure](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile) and internet use low, the general position is inferred rather than measured.

summary: The ministry's own overview names [technology in education as a programme area](2012-07-01-eritrea-moe-overview-of-education); the captured text does not reach what it contains.
developments:
The education ministry's status overview [names information technology in education as a distinct programme area within secondary and general education, alongside technical and vocational training and curriculum reform](2012-07-01-eritrea-moe-overview-of-education). The capture reaches page eleven and not that section, so the repository holds the programme's existence and not its content: no syllabus, no hours, no equipment standard and no school count.

Training that is documented happens outside the school system. A private institute with four branches [graduates roughly 700 a year from technology departments](2026-07-21-shabait-polytech-ai-and-the-future), which is a route outside the secondary curriculum. The [policy for technology in education](2026-09-02-eritrea-technology-education-profile) governs the area without stating its reach.

summary: The engineering college graduated [297 students, a quarter of them women](2026-07-18-eritrea-mai-nefhi-college-297-graduates), including computer science and engineering degrees.
developments:
The nineteenth commencement of the principal engineering college produced [297 graduates, 25 per cent of them women, comprising 289 first degrees including computer science and engineering and eight diplomas including computer application technology and computer hardware and networking technology](2026-07-18-eritrea-mai-nefhi-college-297-graduates). It is the clearest count of a technology cohort the repository has ever held for this country.

Alongside it, a private institute [graduates roughly 700 a year from technology departments, with alumni opening their own technology shops and about 50 graduates in 2026 from new introductory artificial intelligence courses](2026-07-21-shabait-polytech-ai-and-the-future). Those are the two pipelines that can be counted. Where either cohort goes afterwards is not published, and national service assignment governs much of it.

summary: The [2002 proclamation](2002-07-01-estda-establishment-proclamation-122) gives a state agency a research mandate covering information science.
developments:
The legal foundation is strong and dormant. The [2002 proclamation establishes a national science and technology council chaired by the head of state, a development agency and an advisory board, and gives the agency's research office a mandate covering information science and technology, with power to establish research and education institutions in the field](2002-07-01-estda-establishment-proclamation-122). No output of that agency appears on the repository.

What research capacity is visible is delivered from outside — [geospatial workshops run by a regional economic commission](2026-03-01-uneca-eritrea-geospatial-capacity-workshop) — or argued in a [long-form piece making the case for an Eritrean internet gateway, several international routes and domestic hosting](2026-08-10-mesobjournal-eritrea-digital-sovereignty). [Independent domestic publication is itself absent](2026-05-01-rsf-world-press-freedom-index-2026).
qualifier: 2002 agency mandate and a diaspora policy essay only; no domestic research activity on digital policy on record

summary: Participation happens where the government convenes it, as in a [geodesign workshop on water](2026-08-25-eurac-nbs4water-geodesign-asmara). Independent discussion is [absent](2026-05-01-rsf-world-press-freedom-index-2026).
developments:
Two things are true at once. There is convened participation: a [geodesign workshop in the capital brought non-governmental contributors into a planning exercise](2026-08-25-eurac-nbs4water-geodesign-asmara), and the [development programme's annual report describes consultation on the national development plan](2026-06-01-undp-eritrea-annual-report-2025-ndp).

And there is no forum outside that. A [press-freedom index places the country last of 180 for a third consecutive year](2026-05-01-rsf-world-press-freedom-index-2026), and a [commission of inquiry found a surveillance system used to instil fear and keep control](2015-06-05-un-coi-eritrea-detailed-findings-chapter-vi). No independent publication, permitted civil-society body or public forum argues digital or data policy. Participation here means being invited, and nothing in the window changed who does the inviting.
qualifier: No public forum for policy; August geodesign workshop was technical, not an open consultation on an instrument

progress: Movement, in what is measured rather than in access
summary: A quarter of the [engineering college's 297 graduates were women](2026-07-18-eritrea-mai-nefhi-college-297-graduates), and a [June 2026 consultancy](2026-06-11-unesco-iicba-eritrea-emis-data-analytical-support-rfp) requires gender-disaggregated analysis.
developments:
The window produced one count and one commitment to counting. The engineering college's commencement reported [297 graduates with 25 per cent of them women](2026-07-18-eritrea-mai-nefhi-college-297-graduates). The education ministry's consultancy request requires [analysis of teacher deployment and attrition by gender and location](2026-06-11-unesco-iicba-eritrea-emis-data-analytical-support-rfp), naming weak gender disaggregation as one of the faults it is answering.

Behind both sits a register that already disaggregates: the welfare ministry's [vulnerability database collects gender-segregated data](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022). What none of this reaches is access itself. No sex-disaggregated figure for phone ownership, internet use or account holding is published for the country at any date.

summary: A [policy revised in 2021, convention accession in December 2024 and a social protection plan to 2026](2025-10-01-eritrea-fourth-periodic-report-acrwc-disability), with a register behind them.
developments:
The framework is documented in the government's own periodic report: a [national policy for persons with disabilities revised in 2021 with a translation in 2023, accession to the disability rights convention on 20 December 2024, and a national social protection policy and strategic plan for 2022 to 2026](2025-10-01-eritrea-fourth-periodic-report-acrwc-disability). The register behind it is the labour and welfare ministry's [vulnerability database, collecting gender-segregated data on persons with disabilities](2023-04-01-un-eritrea-annual-results-report-2022).

Nothing in it reaches digital access. No accessibility standard governs a public website or service, no assistive-technology provision is described, and the [external committee's July 2026 observations](2026-07-22-acerwc-concluding-observations-eritrea) assess the framework without recording a change to it.
qualifier: disability policy revised 2021 on the state's own report; no ICT or information provision on record

summary: No framework and no accession. The country [is not party to the refugee conventions and has no national protection law](2026-01-01-unhcr-rimap-eritrea-country-profile); displacement runs outward.
developments:
The refugee agency's legal and governance profile records that the country is [not party to the refugee convention, its protocol or the regional refugee convention, has no national legal framework addressing refugee or asylum-seeker protection, and hosts a population of 119 refugees](2026-01-01-unhcr-rimap-eritrea-country-profile).

The displacement that matters here is outward. By December 2025 the agency was aware of [over 679,000 refugees and asylum-seekers from the country worldwide](2026-04-01-unhcr-guidance-note-eritrea), and its [guidance note of April 2026 supersedes eligibility guidelines dating from 2011](2026-04-01-unhcr-guidance-note-eritrea).
qualifier: no refugee framework or convention accession; registration and documents of refugees not described

summary: No programme closing a divide is recorded, and the [grid delivers 52 MW reliably against 74.3 MW of demand](2026-02-01-afdb-energy-integrated-project-appraisal-grid-reliability).
developments:
No programme on the repository is directed at closing a divide. The operator continues [expanding its network](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile), and mobile connections are the only penetration figure published, but nothing states a coverage obligation, a universal-service disbursement or a rural target.

The structural position is unchanged and severe. The [grid delivers 52 MW reliably against 74.3 MW of demand](2026-02-01-afdb-energy-integrated-project-appraisal-grid-reliability), and the [twelve mini-grid centres proposed in answer](2026-01-24-shabait-president-isaias-interview-12-minigrid-energy-plan) have no site or date against them. Electricity comes before access.

summary: A [two-week training in national accounts compilation and a database system](2026-02-24-uneca-eritrea-nadabas-national-accounts-training) was delivered in Eritrea in January 2026. [No statistics law](2007-01-08-norad-eritrea-nso-statistics-norway-mid-term-review) sits under it.
developments:
The training delivered in the country covered [compilation of output by the production approach under the 2008 international standard, and the national accounts database system](2026-02-24-uneca-eritrea-nadabas-national-accounts-training) over two weeks in January 2026. That is methodology and infrastructure together, and it is the most substantial statistical capacity work the repository records.

It has no statutory foundation. A [mid-term review recorded the draft statistical proclamation as submitted and pending in 2007](2007-01-08-norad-eritrea-nso-statistics-norway-mid-term-review), and no later enactment has been located, so the office operates without a statutory mandate. The [population and health survey completed in 2025](2025-09-01-unfpa-eritrea-ephs-2025-data-for-development) is the other half of the picture: capacity being built without a strategy naming what it is for.
qualifier: no NSDS or cited absence on record

summary: Data is produced for the state's own use. The [2025 population and health survey](2025-09-01-unfpa-eritrea-ephs-2025-data-for-development) was to report in 2026, with no dataset released.
developments:
The largest data exercise in fifteen years shows the pattern. The [government-led population and health survey of 2025 was run by the statistics office and the health ministry with an international agency covering half of a US$535,000 budget, as a nationally representative household collection intended to close disaggregated-data gaps for policy and development-goal tracking](2025-09-01-unfpa-eritrea-ephs-2025-data-for-development). Its report was scheduled for 2026; no dataset, licence or catalogue entry accompanies it.

Nothing else on the repository is published as data either. The [geospatial programme](2026-03-01-uneca-eritrea-geospatial-capacity-workshop) produces classified imagery and trained analysts for ministry use, and the only portal recorded is [a basic open data portal noted in a 2022 government-technology dataset](2022-01-01-eritrea-global-digital-identity-index-govtech).
qualifier: basic portal on a 2022 govtech dataset; no licence or dataset published

summary: A [rainfall dataset refreshed every two weeks](2026-07-06-hdx-wfp-eritrea-rainfall-indicators-subnational) and an [August advisory forecasting below-normal rain over the west](2026-08-10-icpac-climate-watch-advisory-dry-conditions). Both are produced abroad.
developments:
Satellite data reaches agriculture here through two external products. A food agency dataset carries [dekadal rainfall indicators computed from satellite precipitation imagery blended with station data and short-term forecasts, aggregated to subnational units and refreshed roughly every two weeks](2026-07-06-hdx-wfp-eritrea-rainfall-indicators-subnational). A regional climate centre's advisory of August 2026 uses [precipitation index analysis with soil-moisture and vegetation-stress monitoring to raise alert levels and forecast below-normal rainfall over the west](2026-08-10-icpac-climate-watch-advisory-dry-conditions).

The domestic side is capacity rather than product: ministry staff trained in [remote sensing, land-cover classification and watershed analysis](2026-03-01-uneca-eritrea-geospatial-capacity-workshop), and an [agricultural expert system](2021-01-16-shabait-agricultural-strategic-information-system-eritrea-ai) reported in 2021. Nothing records a national product built from either.
qualifier: Remote-sensing training for ministry staff; the August satellite advisory is a regional centre's, not a national service

summary: A modern national meteorological service is [listed among forward strategies](2024-12-06-shabait-eritrea-unccd-cop16-statement-meteorological-services), not among institutions. The satellite monitoring that covers the country is [produced abroad](2026-08-10-icpac-climate-watch-advisory-dry-conditions).
developments:
The country's own delegation statement to the desertification convention [lists setting up a modern national meteorological service among its forward strategies](2024-12-06-shabait-eritrea-unccd-cop16-statement-meteorological-services), which places a modern service as an objective rather than an operating institution.

The monitoring itself is external and active. A regional climate centre's advisory of August 2026 uses [precipitation index analysis and soil-moisture and vegetation-stress monitoring to raise alert levels and forecast below-normal rainfall over the west of the country](2026-08-10-icpac-climate-watch-advisory-dry-conditions), and a food agency publishes [satellite-derived rainfall indicators by subnational unit roughly every two weeks](2026-07-06-hdx-wfp-eritrea-rainfall-indicators-subnational). The country is covered; it does not do the covering.
qualifier: Satellite monitoring of the country is produced abroad; a modern national meteorological service is only a planned objective

summary: The foreign minister met a [senior presidential adviser for African affairs](2025-09-26-shabait-osman-saleh-trump-adviser-unga80) in September 2025, discussing renewed engagement including communication and infrastructure.
developments:
The meeting at the general assembly is the first substantive bilateral engagement of the window: the foreign minister and the [United States president's senior adviser for African affairs discussed renewed engagement including trade, investment, infrastructure, transportation, communication and security partnerships](2025-09-26-shabait-osman-saleh-trump-adviser-unga80). It is a conversation rather than an instrument, and nothing has followed it on the repository.

No hyperscaler, cloud provider or technology company engagement of any kind is held for this country, from the United States or anywhere. The reason is structural as much as political: the external country assessment records the [investment centre dormant and the investment law effectively suspended](2025-01-01-us-state-dept-2025-investment-climate-statement-eritrea), so there is no route through which such an engagement would be constituted.

summary: The standing instrument is a [belt and road cooperation memorandum signed in November 2021](2021-11-30-ndrc-china-eritrea-bri-mou-signing). No digital or telecommunications project under it is named.
developments:
The Chinese planning commission's own press release records the founding instrument: a [memorandum on cooperation within the belt and road framework, signed on 24 November 2021 by the Chinese ambassador and the foreign minister](2021-11-30-ndrc-china-eritrea-bri-mou-signing). It has been reaffirmed at leader level since and remains the framework for the relationship.

What the repository cannot show is anything digital passing through it. No telecommunications, data-centre, network or equipment project under the framework is named for this country, and the state operator's [network expansion](2025-01-01-eritrea-digital-watch-country-profile) is not attributed to any foreign partner. Nothing in the window records a new instrument, a project agreement or a disbursement.

summary: The [research and documentation centre, backed by three EU-funded projects, has become a digital-preservation centre](2025-11-13-eeas-research-documentation-center-digital-reality) with training capacity, reported November 2025.
developments:
The engagement that moved is a programme rather than an announcement. The [national research and documentation centre, supported through three successive EU-funded projects and working with an Italian university, is equipped for digitisation and has become a digital-preservation centre with hands-on training capacity, and a draft national archives and libraries law was prepared with its and the university's experts](2025-11-13-eeas-research-documentation-center-digital-reality). The same centre [trained 64 local-institution employees in document management](2025-09-08-shabait-training-documentation-archives) two months earlier, which is what that capacity is for.

No bilateral digital-transformation memorandum exists. The instrument carrying European commitments is the [partnership agreement published in the EU Official Journal in December 2023](2023-12-28-eu-oacps-samoa-agreement), which lists the state among its parties and carries provisions on digital solutions for public access to information and on electronic governance.

summary: One [general cooperation agreement from October 2010](2010-10-19-shabait-eritrea-saudi-cooperation-agreement), covering diverse sectors. No Gulf digital or telecommunications instrument was located.
developments:
The principal Gulf-state relationship rests on a [general cooperation agreement signed in October 2010 between the foreign minister and a Saudi minister of state, covering diverse sectors](2010-10-19-shabait-eritrea-saudi-cooperation-agreement). It is the actual signed instrument that a meeting with a Saudi deputy foreign minister in February 2026 agreed to expedite the implementation of.

Sixteen years on it has produced nothing digital that the repository can see. No dedicated Gulf digital-transformation, telecommunications, data-governance or data-centre memorandum was located for this country, from any Gulf state, and no project under the 2010 agreement is named. What moved in the window was the diplomacy around the instrument rather than the instrument itself.

summary: The standing instrument is the [tele-education and tele-medicine network memorandum of November 2019](2019-11-07-india-eritrea-e-vbab-mou), with an equipped learning centre on site.
developments:
India's principal technology instrument with the country is the [memorandum joining its tele-education and tele-medicine network project, signed on 7 November 2019](2019-11-07-india-eritrea-e-vbab-mou), successor to an earlier pan-African network. It provides tele-education and tele-medicine over India-built portals with an on-site learning centre equipped with computers, an internet connection and audio-visual equipment.

It remains the clearest signed dated technology instrument between the two, and nothing in the window adds to it: no disbursement, no extension, no successor and no enrolment figure. No India-Eritrea instrument on data governance, digital public infrastructure or payments was located, which is notable given how much of India's external technology engagement elsewhere takes that form.
